value.text:
Hongik Technical College (홍익공업전문대학; 弘益工業專門大學) was a private junior college in Mapo District, Seoul, South Korea. It is a closed historical institution, distinct from the Hongik University campus associated with its closure.

The school opened in 1963 as 홍익공예고등전문학교. Its name changed to 홍익공업고등전문학교 in 1967 and to 홍익공업전문학교 in 1971. In 1979 it was reorganized as 홍익공업전문대학. The college closed in 1989 in connection with the establishment of Hongik University’s Jochiwon Campus, now known as Sejong Campus. After closure, the former college building was used as an E-Land Group office. Following the relocation of the company headquarters, the building was demolished for a youth rental housing project.

value.text:
Hongik Technical College (홍익공업전문대학; 弘益工業專門大學) was a private junior college in Mapo District, Seoul, South Korea. It is a closed historical institution, distinct from the Hongik University campus associated with its closure.

The school opened in 1963 as 홍익공예고등전문학교. Its name changed to 홍익공업고등전문학교 in 1967 and to 홍익공업전문학교 in 1971. In 1979 it was reorganized as 홍익공업전문대학. The college closed in 1989 in connection with the establishment of Hongik University’s Jochiwon Campus, now known as Sejong Campus. After closure, the former college building was used as an E-Land Group office. Following the relocation of the company headquarters, the building was demolished for a youth rental housing project.
